title: Database Internals and Performance Engineering
name: 5. Database Internals and Performance Engineering
description: Master relational and log-structured storage engines, 8KB database pages, buffer pool caching and LRU eviction, B+ Trees vs LSM Trees vs Hash indexing, Bloom filters, query parsing, cost-based execution plans, join algorithms (nested loop, hash, sort-merge), transaction ACID guarantees, MVCC tuple versioning, Write-Ahead Logging (WAL), crash recovery (ARIES), table partitioning, and high-availability replication.

quiz.question: What is the primary unit of storage and I/O between persistent disk and memory in PostgreSQL by default?
options: A 64-byte CPU cache line
An 8 KB database page (heap block)
A 1 MB extent
A 128 MB table partition
quiz.explanation: PostgreSQL defaults to 8 KB pages. All table and index I/O is performed in page increments.

quiz.question: Why are B+ Trees preferred over regular B-Trees for relational database indexes?
options: B+ Trees store full table records in all internal nodes
B+ Trees have linked leaf nodes, enabling extremely fast range scans and ordered scans
B+ Trees use O(1) hashing instead of balanced search trees
B+ Trees never require disk I/O
quiz.explanation: In B+ Trees, all actual data pointers are concentrated at the leaf level, and leaves are linked sequentially with sibling pointers for efficient range traversals.

quiz.question: In an LSM Tree architecture, what is the role of a Bloom Filter?
options: To compress SSTables before writing to disk
To quickly test if a key definitely does NOT exist in an SSTable, preventing unnecessary disk I/O
To sort keys inside the active memtable
To coordinate distributed consensus between replicas
quiz.explanation: Bloom filters have zero false negatives: if it says an element is absent, the storage engine can safely skip reading that SSTable file from disk.

quiz.question: When an application executes a query, what is the core responsibility of the Cost-Based Optimizer (CBO)?
options: To write changes to the Write-Ahead Log
To evaluate possible execution plans (scans, joins, orders) and pick the one with the lowest estimated disk/CPU cost
To bill the user's credit card for compute time
To encrypt database tables with AES-256
quiz.explanation: The CBO calculates estimated disk page fetches and CPU tuple costs based on statistics from pg_statistic to select the optimal physical plan.

quiz.question: Which JOIN algorithm builds an in-memory hash table on the smaller inner relation and then streams the larger outer relation?
options: Nested Loop Join
Hash Join
Sort-Merge Join
Broadcast Cartesian Join
quiz.explanation: Hash Join performs a Build Phase (hash table on inner relation in work_mem) followed by a Probe Phase (scanning the outer relation).
